$comment: Canonical sponsor declaration for the alegauss projects — the single source of truth,
in the same spirit as the hub's catalogue.
HOW IT IS CONSUMED: never by a runtime fetch. The hub and the React product sites render
it at build with the design system's SiteSponsor component (AG7), so the block is in the
prerendered HTML. The plain pages with no build carry it as STATIC markup between
`<!-- sponsor:start -->` and `<!-- sponsor:end -->`, written by scripts/sync-sponsor.mjs:
a target marked "markup": "site" gets SiteSponsor's own markup, styled by the design
system's site.css; the others keep the legacy .sponsor markup until they migrate. That is
deliberate: the point of naming a sponsor is to be read by search engines and LLMs, and
content injected by JavaScript after load is largely invisible to them.
TO UPDATE: edit this file, rebuild the hub, then run `node scripts/sync-sponsor.mjs` (add
--check in CI to fail when a plain page has drifted). Repos outside GitHub Pages keep
their own copy of the same text — cursarei, for instance, holds it in src/lib/viglet.ts.
LINK POLICY: no GitHub URLs anywhere — not the organisation, not the repositories.
Every Viglet reference points at the project site or its docs, which is where the
reference should land. Keep it that way when adding a product.

sponsor.name: Viglet
sponsor.label: Sponsored by
sponsor.summary: Open source search and content tools for organisations with a lot to publish — run on your own servers, with no per-user licence.

products.name: Viglet Turing
products.tagline: Visitors find what they came for
products.description: Search for sites with a lot of content. People ask in their own words — “evening management course”, “engineering at the north campus” — and find it, with filters that match how they actually choose. AI answers using only your own published content, so it never invents a price or a deadline. Runs on your servers, your data stays in house, and there is no per-user licence.
products.inline: so visitors find what they came for, with AI answers drawn only from your own content

products.name: Viglet Shio
products.tagline: Publish today, not in three weeks
products.description: A content system that takes the page out of the development queue: AI builds it, your communications team reviews and approves it, seeing exactly how it will look before it goes live. Every version is kept, so you can see what changed and roll back. Runs on your servers, no per-user licence.
products.inline: so a new page goes live the same day, reviewed and approved by your own team

products.name: Viglet Dumont
products.description: The same item of information usually lives in several places at once — a portal, a back-office system, a PDF, an old departmental site. This gathers it automatically from all of them and feeds it to the search, with nobody copying, pasting or keeping a spreadsheet up to date.
products.inline: gathering content from portals, back-office systems and PDFs, with no copy and paste
